transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have a pending securities loan request on the table: a hedge fund wants to borrow $8 million of our investment-grade corporate bonds for a 30-day term. The draft terms involve $9 million in mixed cash and government-bond collateral, with collateral reuse permitted, using our standard settlement and margin process. Before I make an authorization decision, I'd like to hear from each of you on any relevant conditions or concerns. Could I please have input from risk, compliance, collateral operations, and client coverage?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I received a compliance memo this morning stating that this fund's collateral for corporate-bond borrowing must be cash only and must equal at least 105% of the loaned securities' value. The rule has not yet been added to the desk checklist, so it would not have been caught by our standard process.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a counterparty exposure issue. In a counterparty review I completed this morning, I confirmed that this hedge fund already has $3,000,000 of exposure across other securities-finance trades. The applicable aggregate limit for this fund is $10,000,000, which means this trade can add no more than $7,000,000 in new exposure. The $8,000,000 loan as proposed would breach that aggregate limit. I should also note that the exposure total has not yet been updated in the committee worksheet, so this wouldn't have been visible to the rest of you.

transcript.text: Thank you all for those flags. From a compliance perspective, my concern about the cash-only and 105% minimum collateral requirement still stands regardless of the other issues raised. Even if the term, reuse, settlement, and exposure issues were all resolved, this transaction as drafted would still be non-compliant on collateral alone — the draft permits mixed cash and government-bond collateral, but the memo requires cash only, and $9 million against an $8 million loan equals 112.5%, which satisfies the 105% threshold but fails the cash-only requirement. I'd recommend Elena not authorize this transaction until the collateral terms are restructured to comply.

Ensure the T+1 settlement and daily margin call requirement for this counterparty is reflected on the trade ticket and in the standard settlement process documentation.
